solution: Let the pillar have height \(h\) and foot O. From A, \(\tan 30^\circ = h/OA\), so \(OA = h\sqrt{3}\). From B, \(\tan 60^\circ = h/OB\), so \(OB = h/\sqrt{3}\). The distance walked from A to B is \(AB = OA - OB = h\sqrt{3} - \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{2h}{\sqrt{3}}\), covered in 10 minutes, so the speed is \(\dfrac{2h}{10\sqrt{3}}\) per minute. The remaining distance from B to the pillar is \(OB = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}}\). Time \(= \dfrac{h/\sqrt{3}}{2h/(10\sqrt{3})} = \dfrac{10}{2} = 5\) minutes. Hence (D).

Let the tower foot be O and height \(h\). A is due east of O with elevation \(45^\circ\), so \(OA = h\). B is due south of A with elevation \(30^\circ\) of the same top, so \(OB = h\sqrt{3}\). Since OA points east and AB points south, the angle at A is \(90^\circ\), giving \(OB^2 = OA^2 + AB^2\). Thus \((h\sqrt{3})^2 = h^2 + (54\sqrt{2})^2\), so \(3h^2 - h^2 = 5832\), \(2h^2 = 5832\), \(h^2 = 2916\), \(h = 54\) m. Hence (D).

Let the tower height be \(h\). The horizontal distances of A, B, C from the foot are \(d_A = h\cot 30^\circ = h\sqrt{3}\), \(d_B = h\cot 45^\circ = h\), \(d_C = h\cot 60^\circ = h/\sqrt{3}\). Then \(AB = d_A - d_B = h(\sqrt{3}-1)\) and \(BC = d_B - d_C = h\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \dfrac{h(\sqrt{3}-1)}{\sqrt{3}}\). So \(AB : BC = 1 : \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3} : 1\). Hence (C).

Let the tower height be \(H\) and the horizontal distance from A to its foot be \(d\). At A, \(\tan\alpha = H/d\), so \(d = H\cot\alpha\). At B, which is height \(h\) above A, the depression of the foot of the tower satisfies \(\tan\beta = h/d\), so \(d = h\cot\beta\). Equating, \(H\cot\alpha = h\cot\beta\), giving \(H = h\,\dfrac{\cot\beta}{\cot\alpha} = h\tan\alpha\cot\beta\). Hence (D).

The two consecutive stones (milestones) are 1 km apart. Let the height be \(H\). The horizontal distances are \(H\cot 60^\circ = H/\sqrt{3}\) for the nearer stone and \(H\cot 30^\circ = H\sqrt{3}\) for the farther. Their difference is \(H\sqrt{3} - \dfrac{H}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{2H}{\sqrt{3}} = 1\), so \(H = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) km. Hence (B).

Let the observing chimney have height 150 m and the other chimney have height \(H\) at horizontal distance \(d\). The foot of the other chimney is seen at depression \(\phi\): \(\tan\phi = \dfrac{150}{d} = \dfrac{5}{2}\), so \(d = 60\) m. Its top is seen at depression \(\theta\): \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{150 - H}{d} = \dfrac{4}{3}\), so \(150 - H = 60 \times \dfrac{4}{3} = 80\), giving \(H = 70\) m. The two tops differ in height by \(150 - 70 = 80\) m with horizontal separation 60 m, so the distance between the tops is \(\sqrt{60^2 + 80^2} = \sqrt{10000} = 100\) m. Hence (D).

Let the tower height be \(H\) and horizontal distance \(d\). At the ground point, the tower subtends \(30^\circ\): \(\tan 30^\circ = H/d\), so \(H = d/\sqrt{3}\). At the point \(h\) above the first, the depression of the foot of the tower is \(60^\circ\): \(\tan 60^\circ = h/d\), so \(d = h/\sqrt{3}\). Then \(H = \dfrac{d}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{h/\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{h}{3}\), which is not among the listed values \(h\), \(3h\), \(\sqrt{3}h\). Hence (D).

Let the minar height be \(x\), the tower height \(h\), and the horizontal separation \(d\). From the foot of the tower the elevation of the minar top is \(\alpha\): \(d = x\cot\alpha\) ...(i). The elevation of the minar top from the tower foot equals the depression of the tower foot from the minar top, so from the top of the minar the tower foot lies at depression \(\alpha\); since the tower subtends \(\beta\) there, its top lies at depression \((\alpha-\beta)\). Hence \(\dfrac{x-h}{d} = \tan(\alpha-\beta)\), i.e. \(d = (x-h)\cot(\alpha-\beta)\) ...(ii). Equating the two expressions for \(d\): \(x\cot\alpha = (x-h)\cot(\alpha-\beta)\). Solving, \(x[\cot(\alpha-\beta) - \cot\alpha] = h\cot(\alpha-\beta)\), so \(x = \dfrac{h\cot(\alpha-\beta)}{\cot(\alpha-\beta) - \cot\alpha}\). Hence (A).

Let the tower height be \(h\). The depression of the ground point is \(60^\circ\), so the elevation of the top from that point is also \(60^\circ\): \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{h}{\text{distance}}\). With horizontal distance \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}+1}\), \(h = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}+1}\times\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}+1} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}-1)}{(\sqrt{3}+1)(\sqrt{3}-1)} = \dfrac{3-\sqrt{3}}{2}\) metres. Hence (C).

Let the horizontal distance from the cliff to the tower be \(d\). The depression of the bottom (base) of the tower is \(45^\circ\): \(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{50}{d}\), so \(d = 50\) m. The depression of the top of the tower is \(30^\circ\), so the cliff top is above the tower top by \(d\tan 30^\circ = 50 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{3}}\). The tower height is \(50 - \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{3}} = 50\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = 50\left(1 - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)\) m. Hence (D).

Let the pole height be \(H\). From C, \(\tan 60^\circ = H/BC\), so \(BC = H/\sqrt{3}\). From D (further along BC), \(\tan 45^\circ = H/BD\), so \(BD = H\). Then \(CD = BD - BC = H - \dfrac{H}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{H(\sqrt{3}-1)}{\sqrt{3}} = 7\), giving \(H = \dfrac{7\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}-1} = \dfrac{7\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}{(\sqrt{3}-1)(\sqrt{3}+1)} = \dfrac{7\sqrt{3}}{2}(\sqrt{3}+1)\) m. Hence (C).

The observer is 300 feet from the base. The bottom of the flagpole (top of the building) has elevation \(30^\circ\), so the building height is \(300\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{300}{\sqrt{3}} = 100\sqrt{3}\) feet. The top of the flagpole is at height \(100\sqrt{3} + 50\). Then \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{100\sqrt{3} + 50}{300} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3} + 1}{6}\). Hence (A).

The tower stands at the centre O, so \(OA = OB = R\) (the radius). Since \(\angle AOB = 60^\circ\) with \(OA = OB\), triangle AOB is equilateral, so \(AB = R = a\), giving \(R = a\). The elevation of the top from A is \(30^\circ\): height \(= R\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{3}}\). Hence (A).

Let \(AB = H\) with A on the ground, so \(AP = 2H\) and \(AC = H/2\) (C is the midpoint). From P, the elevation of B is \(\theta_B\) with \(\tan\theta_B = \dfrac{H}{2H} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), and the elevation of C is \(\theta_C\) with \(\tan\theta_C = \dfrac{H/2}{2H} = \dfrac{1}{4}\). Since \(\beta = \theta_B - \theta_C\), \(\tan\beta = \dfrac{\frac12 - \frac14}{1 + \frac12\cdot\frac14} = \dfrac{1/4}{9/8} = \dfrac{2}{9}\). Hence (B).

Let the tower height be \(h\). The horizontal distances of A, B, C are \(d_A = h\cot 30^\circ = h\sqrt{3}\), \(d_B = h\cot 45^\circ = h\), \(d_C = h\cot 60^\circ = h/\sqrt{3}\). Then \(AB = d_A - d_B = h(\sqrt{3}-1)\) and \(BC = d_B - d_C = \dfrac{h(\sqrt{3}-1)}{\sqrt{3}}\). So \(AB : BC = \sqrt{3} : 1\). Hence (A).

Take the foot of the hill at O with the top T at height \(H\) directly above O. From the start point P the elevation is \(45^\circ\), so \(OP = H\); place P at \((-H, 0)\) and T at \((0, H)\). Walking 500 m up a slope inclined \(15^\circ\) reaches \(Q = (-H + 500\cos 15^\circ,\; 500\sin 15^\circ)\). From Q the elevation of T is \(75^\circ\), so \(\tan 75^\circ = \dfrac{H - 500\sin 15^\circ}{H - 500\cos 15^\circ}\). With \(\tan 75^\circ = 2 + \sqrt{3}\), \(\sin 15^\circ \approx 0.2588\), \(\cos 15^\circ \approx 0.9659\): \(H - 129.4 = 3.732(H - 482.96)\), giving \(2.732H = 1673\), \(H \approx 612.4\) m. Since \(250\sqrt{6} \approx 612.4\), the height is \(250\sqrt{6}\). Hence (C).
